title: Process-safety leading/lagging metrics as barrier-health visibility rail
summary: This record encodes process-safety metrics as a visibility rail: leading indicators, lagging indicators, near misses, operating discipline, and layers-of-protection performance can make barrier health visible before catastrophe, but metric choice and governance can also mislead.

place.scope: United States / professional process-safety infrastructure unless otherwise stated

claims.claim: CCPS describes process safety metrics as part of the Learning from Experience pillar and says leading/lagging indicators help companies monitoring hazardous materials evaluate trends, continuously monitor and improve process-safety programs, and reduce process-safety risks.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: OSHA’s metrics fact sheet says metrics are used to evaluate and track a facility’s PSM program performance and identify improvements for facilities handling highly hazardous chemicals.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: OSHA distinguishes lagging metrics gathered after severity-threshold incidents from leading metrics that reveal performance of key work processes, operating discipline, and layers of protection before a major process-safety incident occurs; it also cautions that metrics should be facility/culture specific.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

limitations: Does not establish completeness, compliance, adoption, or effectiveness.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: leading/lagging indicators, near-miss/event thresholds, work-process and layer-of-protection performance metrics, facility-specific trend monitoring
limitations: metric adoption/effectiveness must be audited case by case
poorly chosen metrics can become target proxies or hide major hazard risk
professional guidance is not the same as regulation or compliance

handling_notes: Infrastructure records describe visibility/correction rails, not proof that accidents are prevented.
Regulatory/program descriptions must be rechecked before policy or compliance use.
